stem:
You perform a rapid FAST scan in resuscitation, confirming a significant amount of abdominal free fluid. The surgical team remain concerned about going straight to theatre.

Which one of the following is the next best step in the definitive management of Penny?

options.text: Transfer to theatre for emergency exploratory laparotomy

explanation: In a child with major blunt trauma, haemodynamic instability, and a FAST scan showing significant intraperitoneal free fluid, the definitive management is urgent operative control of likely intra-abdominal bleeding. CT is for stable patients; delaying surgery for further fluid alone or inotropes is inappropriate.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Trauma 2 - Pain

rationale: The source question asks for definitive management. A positive FAST with significant free fluid in a trauma patient with concerning physiology implies intra-abdominal haemorrhage requiring urgent operative control.

optionExplanations.A: PICU may be needed after source control, but it is not the definitive next step for haemoperitoneum with suspected ongoing bleeding.
optionExplanations.B: CT abdomen with contrast is generally reserved for haemodynamically stable trauma patients, not those with significant free fluid and concerning physiology.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: significant free fluid on FAST in the setting of major trauma and likely ongoing bleeding warrants emergency exploratory laparotomy.
optionExplanations.D: Further fluids alone do not address the bleeding source and can delay definitive management.
optionExplanations.E: Inotropes may temporise circulation but do not treat haemorrhagic shock from internal bleeding and are not definitive management.

The following text applies to the questions at positions 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15

Clinical scenario 2 - Penny

Teaching/Learning points:

Cardiovascular assessment

Physiological differences in children with shock

Approach to resuscitation / fluids

Blood on the floor… and four more (chest, abdomen, pelvis and long bone).

The emergency department receives an advanced warning from the ambulance service of a high-speed motor vehicle collision on the motorway nearby. At least three cars are involved and there have been a number of fatalities. Fire rescue services and a pre-hospital medical retrieval team are on the scene as a number of casualties are trapped and require extrication.

Your unit will be receiving

Penny,

a three year old female, who was found at the roadside some five metres from the main scene. It is thought she was ejected from one of the vehicles involved, in which two adult occupants died at the scene. She has been intubated at the scene due to reduced conscious level.

Vital signs are:

Respiratory rate 25bpm (ventilated)

Saturations 98% in 50% oxygen

Heart rate 120bpm

Blood Pressure 95/40.

She has multiple abrasions over her face and torso. ETA is 15 minutes...

The following nine questions refer to Penny’s clinical scenario.
